purpose: Teach: 分かれる/目立ち/気がつか/ゆかり/枯れ/残ら/落とさ/贈る

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 人生の道、分かれる時、勇気が要ったな。
lines.en: It took courage when life's paths would fork.
lines.style: Slow, measured opening. Voice settles into quietness. Gaze turned inward. Not sad—exactly, but weighted with years of those choices. A pause between thoughts, like he's still there at those crossroads.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。私の若い頃、目立ちたい時もあったわよ。
lines.en: Yes. When I was young, there were times I wanted to stand out too.
lines.style: Gentle agreement that carries understanding. A small smile in the voice. Not mournful—almost amused at her younger self. Trails off softly on the admission, like she's sharing something she's kept quiet about.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 最近、足元、気がつかないと、危ない。
lines.en: Lately, if you don't watch where you're stepping, things get dangerous.
lines.style: Quiet dry humor, a touch of wisdom. Matter-of-fact but not unkind. Almost a gentle warning wrapped in acceptance. The hint of a smile underneath the practicality.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖母ちゃんゆかりの古本、整理しなきゃ。
lines.en: I really should organize your grandmother's old books one of these days.
lines.style: Soft, half-formed thought aloud. A gentle hesitation—duty mixed with affection. Voice lingers on the word 'organize' like she's holding the memory of those books in her hands, not quite ready to let them go.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 庭の盆栽、枯れさせないよう、毎日水を。
lines.en: The bonsai in the garden—I water them every day so they won't wither.
lines.style: Simple, deliberate statement. Voice carries the quiet routine of care. Not sentimental—just matter-of-fact about tending what matters. Each word given its own small weight.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お料理、残らないように、お互い少しずつね。
lines.en: With the cooking, we both keep portions small so nothing goes to waste.
lines.style: Warm, practical wisdom. The voice of someone who has learned to not take more than necessary. Soft at the edges, almost conspiratorial—like this is the little kindness they've worked out together.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、お前を駅まで送って、落とさず帰したな。
lines.en: When I was young, I'd walk you all the way to the station and see you home safely.
lines.style: Voice softens into genuine tenderness. The memory surfaces quietly—not to boast, but to hold. Pace slows as he speaks, like he's back there for a moment. Small, true smile underneath.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 息子に、人生の本を贈るのも、いいかしらね。
lines.en: Maybe I should give our son a book about life—something like that.
lines.style: Thoughtful, half-forming the idea as she speaks. Warm consideration underneath. Voice rises slightly at the question-mark—seeking gentle agreement more than asking permission. Genuinely wondering if this small gift might matter.
